approachQuestion.prompt:
Prime station labels

Return the number of primes in inclusive [2,N]. A prime has exactly two positive divisors. An empty range has count zero.

Example 1: N=10 -> 4, for 2,3,5,7.
Example 2: N=1 -> 0.
Example 3: N=2 -> 1.

Constraints and assumptions: 1 <= N <= 10000000. A boolean table indexed through N is permitted. Return only the count. Choose the best time bound among the offered correct methods, then the least auxiliary storage when time ties.

options.text: Initialize a boolean table through N with 0 and 1 false. For each still-prime p with p*p<=N, clear multiples starting at p*p. Count true entries.
options.feedback: Every composite has a prime divisor at most its square root; smaller multiples of p were already cleared by smaller primes.

options.text: For each candidate 2 through N, test divisors through its integer square root, stopping at the first divisor. Count those with none.
options.feedback: Each test is valid, but divisibility work is repeated instead of shared across the range.

options.text: For each flagged p, clear p,2p,3p,...; then count flags.
options.feedback: It clears the prime itself; N=2 gives zero instead of one.

options.text: Count 2 and all odd integers above 2 as prime.
options.feedback: At N=9 this also counts the composite 9.

feedback.reason: Share composite elimination across a bounded range.
details: Initialize N+1 flags to true except 0 and 1. For each still-flagged p with p*p<=N, clear p*p,p*p+p,... through N. Count remaining flags.

Start marking at p*p because smaller multiples already have a smaller prime factor. Only still-flagged p launches a marking pass. The Boolean table is helper storage even when the answer is only a count.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (sieve-count). Let N be the endpoint. Include table initialization and final scanning. Choose its tightest standard worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
Include initialization and any copying; no hidden preprocessing or cache.

options.text: O(N log log N) time, O(N) auxiliary space
O(N sqrt(N)) time, O(1) auxiliary space
O(N log log N) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Sieve marking sums prime-multiple visits, with an N+1 flag table.
details: Ordinary sieve marking sums N/p over primes p up to sqrt(N), giving the tight standard asymptotic bound O(N log log N). Initialization and scanning add linear work. The N+1 flags dominate auxiliary storage.
Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
“O(N log log N) time, O(N) auxiliary space”: Correct for this ordinary sieve.
“O(N) time, O(N) auxiliary space”: Repeated clearing by different primes prevents this bound for the stated sieve.
“O(N sqrt(N)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This describes separate trial division rather than shared flags.
“O(N log log N) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The table counts as auxiliary state, since only the count is returned.
